comments.author: @2175Wook
comments.text:
I think considering the time they mapped out the borders, with the technology they had they did do a good job of trying to keep the borders as straight as possible.

Zooming in at Four Corners Monument by Colorado bottom border with Utah, there is a an angle border that moves 25 metres off from a vertical line.

comments.author: @2175Wook
comments.text:
This is an interesting way to look at Colorado in terms of its borders.

I see that that curvature of earth would mean that bottom border would be a bit longer with the curve.

I looked at a part of Colorado border with Kansas on google maps.
Looking for curves in the border, when I zoomed in at the border with Colorado and Kansas, around 60 km above Oklahoma Border. 
I can see by W Rd 12 , that there is an angled border that separate 2 straight lines.
A point I want to make is that it only separates the 2 straight lines by around 20 metres.
So, this is why I am thinking with the 697 times these border lines change,, the changes are very minor over the whole border length. This is why the border appears straight when you view Colorado at a glance.
I guess it can be seen as a trapezium in shape because of the earth curvature and it is only when you zoom in that the border very slightly changes not by much.
